title: [CQ-V01a] Protected check definition shape
description:
Objective: define the structured, approval-bound shape of a protected required check: the definition an architect approves. It is consumed by CQ-V01b (task-db57e0148a9d47839c4159aab8a8c16d) and by CQ-V01 (task-bde8654052f648f9b209174c3708322b), which was split by SPIDR because a single slice would exceed QA's 400-line cap. This task supersedes task-80f76f99cca64dc1909765af71977e46, archived before any work because its DoD contradicted the code.

Deliverable: a producer contract. Later slices consume these exact names.

types/schema.ts:
- `ProtectedCheckDefinition = { id: string; command: string; configs?: string[]; scripts?: string[]; assertionRoots?: string[] }`.
- `TaskExecutionContract.requiredChecks?: ProtectedCheckDefinition[]`, appended after checkRefs in the canonical F03 key order. checkRefs stays as it is.

state/validators.ts: validateExecutionContract validates requiredChecks strictly and losslessly (no truncation). It refuses with INVALID_INPUT naming the exact field.
- At most 20 definitions.
- id: 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9._-], starting alphanumeric, unique.
- command: non-blank, single line, at most 1000 chars, kept exactly as given (the command as the runner will run it).
- Every path list: at most 50 entries, each through normalizeAffectedFile (no globs, traversal or absolute paths), deduplicated in first-seen order.
- Unknown keys are refused; empty lists are omitted.
- The contract is already approval-material. A non-submission write that changes requiredChecks advances planRevision through the existing F03 derivation, unchanged. Every PLAN_SUBMITTED advances it anyway.

New pure module packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.ts:
- definitionDigest(defs): lowercase sha256 hex of the canonical JSON of validated definitions. Key order is id, command, configs, scripts, assertionRoots; lists stay as stored.
- protectedPaths(defs): the sorted, deduplicated union of every path list, each path with its kind.

tools/submitPlan.ts: the inputSchema declares requiredChecks inside executionContract.

NOT in scope:
- measuring file content, or any Git read (CQ-V01b);
- candidate protected entries, the delivery predicate and get_context (CQ-V01);
- running checks;
- docs (held for CQ-V12);
- verified-local.
Contracts without requiredChecks behave exactly as today.

Verification (fresh, exit 0 required): cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test
definitionOfDone: validateExecutionContract accepts valid requiredChecks losslessly: paths normalized, deduplicated first-seen, empty lists omitted. It refuses each invalid shape with INVALID_INPUT naming the exact field: over 20 definitions; a bad or duplicate id; a blank, multiline or oversized command; an unnormalized, glob, absolute or traversal path; over 50 paths; an unknown key. Proven by new vitest cases.

submit_plan accepts executionContract.requiredChecks through its inputSchema and persists it. An updateTask write that changes only requiredChecks advances planRevision. One that writes equal definitions (same values, keys in another order) does not. Proven by new vitest cases.

definitionDigest is deterministic: equal definitions give the same digest, and any changed id, command or path gives a different one. protectedPaths returns the sorted, deduplicated union with each path's kind. Proven by unit tests.

Contracts without requiredChecks behave exactly as before, and every existing F03 contract test still passes. The only edits to those tests extend the two pinned allowlists (the FIELDS constant and the submit_plan schema parity check) with requiredChecks. No assertion is removed or weakened.
Fresh `cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test` exits 0, and its output is supplied to complete_task.

implementationPlan.description:
New pure module packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/requiredChecks.ts. Its only imports are node:crypto and types: no state, no I/O.

- `export function definitionDigest(defs: readonly ProtectedCheckDefinition[]): string` returns the lowercase sha256 hex of `JSON.stringify(defs.map(d => [d.id, d.command, d.configs ?? [], d.scripts ?? [], d.assertionRoots ?? []]))`. Tuples make key order irrelevant. The input is the VALIDATED contract value.
- `export type ProtectedPathKind = 'configs' | 'scripts' | 'assertionRoots'`.
- `export function protectedPaths(defs): { path: string; kind: ProtectedPathKind }[]` returns unique (path, kind) pairs, sorted by path and then by kind in that order.
- The header comment says that V01b (snapshot measurement) and V01 (the delivery predicate) consume these, and that a digest is never accepted from a caller as evidence.
implementationPlan.note: Pure helpers implemented in 22 lines using node:crypto, Set and deterministic code-unit sort only; no state/I/O dependencies or evidence acceptance. Approved tuple digest encoding pinned by test. Helper tests: 8 passed/110 filtered, exit 0; /tmp/moe-v01a-helpers.fdropbve/verification.log. Digest binds each field, kind and stored list order; path union preserves distinct (path,kind) pairs. Ponytail loaded; stdlib covers requested scope.

implementationPlan.description:
submit_plan, in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/submitPlan.ts.

1. inputSchema: add requiredChecks to `executionContract.properties`, after checkRefs, so the parity check's key order matches EXECUTION_CONTRACT_FIELDS.
   - Shape: `{ type: 'array', maxItems: MAX_REQUIRED_CHECKS, items: { type: 'object', additionalProperties: false, required: ['id', 'command'], properties: { id (maxLength 64), command (maxLength MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_COMMAND_CHARS), configs, scripts and assertionRoots (each an array, maxItems MAX_REQUIRED_CHECK_PATHS, string items) } }, description: 'Protected required checks: approved commands plus the config/script files and assertion roots whose content defines them; changes advance planRevision.' }`.
2. Rail scan (~350): today it builds contract text with `Object.values(executionContract).flat().join(' ')`. That turns definition objects into '[object Object]' and skips their text.
   - Collect strings instead: every text and list value, plus each requiredChecks id, command and path.
   - Required patterns still come only from the steps (the F03 decision).
   - Error handling is unchanged: assertPlanRails throws before any write.

Run the focused tests from step 1 until they pass.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: requiredChecks becomes a ninth executionContract key. Approval materiality, every-writer validation and get_context exposure then come from the F03 machinery for free, with no new revision authority. Rejected: a top-level Task field, which would need its own planRevision term in derivePlanRevision plus a second submit_plan parameter, duplicating F03. Rejected: adding requiredChecks to the F03 test's FIELDS constant, which drives string-only per-field cases. The digest uses positional tuples, so key order can never change it.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- validators.ts: CONTRACT_FIELD_KINDS drives EXECUTION_CONTRACT_FIELDS, which drives unknown-key refusal and iteration. rejectUnknownFields reports the bare key, so nested definitions need their own dotted field.
- normalizeAffectedFile collapses ./, // and backslashes but allows globs, hence the extra glob/pathspec check.
- taskStore derivePlanRevision deep-compares the contract (sameSanitizedSurface, key-order-insensitive). Every PLAN_SUBMITTED bumps the revision, so materiality is proven through updateTask.
- submitPlan: the executionContract inputSchema has additionalProperties false, and the rail scan flattens values with .flat().join(' '), which breaks for objects.
- state/executionContract.test.ts: FIELDS (lines 11-12) feeds the it.each cases at 62/128/196; the allowlist assertion is at 155 and the schema parity check at 216.
- schema.ts and validators.ts are CRLF today; dependency task-709f6691 renormalizes them.
planningNotes.risks:
- The allowlist test edit must be exactly one line (~155). Touching FIELDS breaks F03's string cases and violates DoD 4.
- The rail scan bug would let forbidden text hide in a check command if the flatten is left as is.
- V01b (snapshot) and V01 (predicate) consume definitionDigest and protectedPaths under these exact names. Renaming them breaks the split contract.
